title: Principal Firmware Engineer
jobDescription:
Overview

Microsoft Silicon and Cloud Hardware Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Skype, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with its server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering trusted experiences to customers and partners worldwide, and we are looking for passionate engineers to help achieve that mission.    

Are you passionate about working on cutting edge technology in a team that embodies the growth mindset? Are you hoping to join an organization which is built on the mission “To empower every person and organization on this planet to achieve more”?  

The Firmware Center of Excellence org in SCHIE is responsible for building Hardware/Firmware for Azure Infrastructure. We are working on the next generation of Hardware/Firmware for server, silicon, and rack infrastructure with a focus on innovation in firmware technology to secure Azure infrastructure for Microsoft and their customers. Our team works closely with AI and Azure-Core teams for the architecture and development of Cobalt and Maia systems in Azure Data-centre. 

We are looking for a highly motivated Principal Firmware Engineer with a strong background in silicon firmware library and Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) development for embedded systems. In this role you will define the architecture of the reusable firmware libraries, HAL, and low-level device drivers that enable the bring-up and operation of Microsoft’s next-generation AI and compute silicon.  

 #SCHIE 



Responsibilities

  • Drive the architectural vision and strategic direction for silicon firmware libraries and the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) across SoC platforms—spanning boot ROMs, low-level device drivers, and system runtimes. Define reusable driver interfaces (like- PCIe, NVME, Memory Controller, Network Interface) and the system libraries required for SoC bring-up, ensuring scalability, portability, performance, and security. 

  • Mentor and guide senior and junior engineers in firmware library, HAL, and driver development, debugging, and optimization. Provide technical oversight across multiple subsystems and components. 

  • Serve as the primary technical liaison between hardware/silicon architects, Silicon DV team and partner firmware development teams to align silicon firmware library and HAL development with overall product goals. 

  • Lead complex system-level debugging efforts, conduct root cause analysis, and perform performance tuning across the hardware, HAL, and firmware boundaries. 

  • Evaluate emerging technologies and industry trends in silicon firmware, HAL design, and low-level software. Propose and prototype innovative solutions to enhance reusability, portability, and operational efficiency across product lines. 

  • Own the complete firmware library development lifecycle—from concept and design through SoC bring-up, validation, manufacturing, and productization. Ensure delivery of high-quality, production-ready, reusable code. 



Qualifications

Required Qualifications  

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, Computer Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related field.

  • 12+ years of professional years of Experience in FW and or Embedded SW development experience, particularly in a multi-core platform environment with a strong focus on  scalable architecture.  

  • 8+ years of experience designing and developing Hardware Abstraction Layers (HAL), reusable silicon firmware libraries, and low-level device drivers (PCIe, SPI, I2C, I3C, or similar) for SoC platforms, including driver interface definition and system libraries for SoC bring-up. 

  • Solid understanding of computer architectures including processors, buses, and memories.  

  • Proven track record of leading complex SoC bring-up initiatives, collaborating across multiple stakeholder teams, and delivering production-grade firmware solutions. 

  • Expert-level proficiency in C/C++/Rust, with demonstrated experience in designing and optimizing low-level firmware components.  

Preferred Qualifications  

  • Knowledge of operating systems including drivers, memory management, boot loaders, and scheduling. 

  • Basic Verilog (or any other HDL) programming & waveform debugging 

  • Excellent debugging skills with GDB or equivalent. 

  • Experience developing firmware in pre-silicon environments and on test benches. 

  • Shipped products running firmware or embedded software you’ve written. 

  • Experience with one or more of these: drivers, DMA, PCIe, NVMe, image video encoders/decoders, memory controllers/training, boot flows, or power management 

  • Deep understanding of computer architecture, including processors, buses, memory hierarchies, and interconnects.

title: Software Engineering Manager (AI-native development)
jobDescription:
Overview

If you love the pursuit of excellence and are inspired by the challenges that come through driving innovations that impact how the world lives, works and plays, then we invite you to learn more about Microsoft Business Operations (MBO) - and the value we deliver across Microsoft and to our customers and partners. We offer unique opportunities to work on interesting global projects in an environment that appreciates diversity, focuses on talent development and recognizes and rewards great work.

 

As a Software Engineering Manager, you’ll support, coach, and lead the teams that build and operate the platforms powering how Microsoft does business - growing engineers, driving delivery, and solving complex, high-impact problems at global scale.

Position Description

As a Software Engineering Manager, you will lead a team of engineers to design, develop, and operate software solutions across a set of products and services, while owning the growth, development, and performance of the people on your team. You will partner with product managers, technical leads, and cross-functional stakeholders to confirm customer and business requirements and guide your team in translating them into secure, reliable, scalable, and maintainable solutions.

 

You will lead the disciplined use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and practices across the software development lifecycle, ensuring your team takes responsibility for the content of its AI-generated artifacts and integrates Responsible AI practices. You will own and lead architecture discussions and complex design reviews, guide test strategy and security testing, manage dependencies across teams, and uphold Microsoft standards of security, privacy, safety, and accessibility. As a people manager, you will model our culture, coach your team, and care for each individual - driving employee growth and development, executing projects, and managing performance.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

Responsibilities

As a Software Engineering Manager, you will lead across the engineering lifecycle for a set of products and services - guiding your team to design, code, test, deploy, and operate solutions that are secure, reliable, accessible, and maintainable - while delivering success through your people. You will own architecture decisions, drive project planning, lead the disciplined use of AI tools across the development lifecycle, and manage the growth, development, and performance of your engineers.

  • People management. Deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching, and caring - live our culture and values, define team objectives and outcomes, enable success across boundaries, and help the team adapt and learn. Attract and retain great people, know each individual’s capabilities and aspirations, and invest in the growth of others while driving employee development, project execution, and performance management.
  • AI-native development. Lead your team in the disciplined use of AI tools and practices across the full software development lifecycle, ensuring engineers take responsibility for the content of their AI-generated artifacts and incorporate Responsible AI practices. Coach the team on applying engineering health measures (e.g., Accelerate, SPACE, Engineering System Success Playbook) to improve processes, and champion experimentation with new AI tools and practices.
  • Coding. Guide your team within and across teams to produce extensible, maintainable, well-tested, secure, and performant code that adheres to design specifications. Lead efforts to continuously improve code performance, testability, maintainability, and cost; provide deep expertise on coding and validation strategy; and lead the identification and escalation of blockers, communicating how they impact timelines.
  • Code reviews. Coach engineers to review product and test code for team standards, correct test coverage, coding patterns, security risks, compliance issues, and best practices. Conduct timely reviews that accelerate the team’s pace, consider diagnosability, reliability, testability, and maintainability, and ensure automated source-code analysis is built into the development process.
  • Design and architecture. Own and lead architecture discussions and design decisions for complex products and solutions, testing and exploring design options, outlining strengths and weaknesses, and recommending the best approach. Create and review architecture and design documents, evaluate new technologies, and ensure designs meet performance, scalability, resiliency, disaster recovery, cost (COGS), security, and privacy requirements. Review complex designs within and across teams to recommend improvements.
  • Testing and quality. Guide your team in creating clear test strategies that ensure solution quality and prevent regression, incorporating security testing to validate security invariants (including negative cases). Lead efforts to close test gaps, improve suite speed, reliability, and defect localization, ensure testable code, and leverage AI tools for test automation.
  • Customer requirements. Guide partnership with internal and external stakeholders (e.g., product managers, privacy/security subject matter experts, technical leads, customer escalation teams) to confirm customer and user requirements and their feasibility. Leverage a variety of feedback channels to incorporate customer insights into current and future designs, and advocate for the security and privacy needs of customers.
  • Dependencies and coordination. Lead the identification of dependencies and incorporate them into design documents, demonstrating deep understanding of upstream and downstream interactions across the entire stack. Negotiate across teams to resolve conflicts over dependency ownership and required work, and drive agreements that align dependent teams to the delivery schedule.
  • Planning and implementation. Drive multiple groups’ project plans, release plans, and work items in coordination with stakeholders (e.g., technical program managers). Break long-term vision into milestones, guide estimation, anticipate future goals to plan resources, and ensure security, privacy, and compliance requirements are accounted for in planning, including capacity, failover, and backup/restore for disaster recovery.
  • Deployment and velocity. Act as an expert in safe deployment, establishing standards and following safe-change practices to minimize adverse impact to users. Drive comprehensive deployment automation targeting zero-touch deployment, ensure a CI/CD infrastructure that promotes developer and operational agility, monitor dependency status so only the latest secure versions ship, and define when rollback plans should be enacted.
  • Experimentation. Guide team experiments that determine the effectiveness of changes using feature flags and flighting, ensuring the correct telemetry is in place, interpreting results, and making ship decisions. Ensure engineers have time and resources to experiment, and drive collaboration with internal partners (e.g., Data Science, product managers) to incorporate success and guard-rail metrics.
  • Engineering excellence. Act as an expert in best practices and secure design principles, building code on well-established methods and formally validating security invariants. Guide tool development and responsible reuse of open-source and internal code, advocate for GenAI tooling to enhance engineering productivity, and keep the team’s skills current through learning sessions and evaluation of new trends, technical solutions, and patterns.
  • Live site and reliability. Guide your team as designated responsible individuals (DRIs), leading on-call coverage, incident response, and retrospectives that identify root causes and repair actions using least-privilege access. Establish playbooks, guidelines, and processes; ensure responses meet SLA; drive reductions in incident volume and severity; and champion a live-site-first mentality with comprehensive observability and monitoring.
  • Telemetry and monitoring. Integrate, design, and review logging and instrumentation across the team to gather telemetry on performance, reliability, availability, utility, and safety, and to support security investigation for both live and A/B experiments. Lead the classification and analysis of complex data, drive outputs (e.g., notifications, dashboards) that improve monitoring, and coach the team on the privacy implications of telemetry changes.
  • Security, privacy, and compliance. Coach the team to apply security best practices and model “security as code,” incorporating deployment gates, scanners, and security monitoring to prevent regressions and vulnerabilities. Collaborate with security partners to define security promises and invariants, validate threat models and premortems, and establish breach drills and incident response. Ensure the correct processes for privacy, safety, and accessibility, maintain visible evidence of compliance, and stay current on global and local regulations.
  • Collaboration and communication. Communicate clearly and respectfully - verbally and in writing - to drive collaborative, mutually beneficial outcomes; negotiate and resolve conflict across teams; and contribute to an inclusive culture and a growth mindset.

  • Hands-on experience using artificial intelligence (AI) tools and practices across the software development lifecycle in a disciplined manner, taking responsibility for the content of AI-generated changes to artifacts and reviewing all changes.

title: Product Manager
jobDescription:
Overview

Customer Success Engineering (CSE) sits within CEAI and builds the AI-powered platforms, applications, and agents that transform how Microsoft engages, retains, and grows its customers. If you’re excited to build, experiment, and shape the future of commercial execution with AI at the core, we invite you to apply. 

We are looking for a Product Manager who is equal parts Product Strategist and hands-on AI Builder. This is an AI-native product role: you won’t just define what to build — you’ll use AI to build it. You will set the strategy for the next wave of AI solutions across Microsoft’s Customer Success motion, then rapidly prototype and ship those solutions yourself using AI-assisted development. This role blends two operating modes. Great candidates are strong in both — and comfortable moving between them daily: 

Product Strategist 

  • Owns the multi-quarter vision and roadmap for AI-first applications. 
  • Frames the problem spaces, defines the bets, and sequences the portfolio. 
  • Translates business goals into measurable product outcomes. 
  • Aligns leaders, engineering, and design around a shared strategy

AI Builder

  • Uses AI to build — prototypes and ships applications, agents, and workflows. 
  • Turns concepts into working demos in days, not quarters. 
  • Instruments builds with telemetry and evals for AI quality and impact. 
  • Raises team throughput by applying AI to the product-development loop. 

 

Your work will directly impact multi-billion-dollar businesses — fueling revenue growth, sharpening competitive advantage, and optimizing margins. You will also push the latest AI frontiers, including autonomous agentic workflows, deep research and reasoning, and multi-agent frameworks, while maintaining a relentless focus on high-quality user experiences — from conversational UX to emerging interaction models across the Microsoft and Copilot ecosystem. Just as importantly, you will use AI to raise the productivity of the entire product organization, establishing the tools, patterns, and evals that let the team ship better products, faster. 

This role reflects how product management is evolving in CSE — from requirements author to builder and decision architect. We look for people who consistently demonstrate four shifts: 

  • Builder, not just author. Move beyond specifications to build lightweight business models, decision flows, prototypes, and AI-assisted experiments that stakeholders can evaluate before engineering commits — using AI-assisted development to check in production-ready code for enhancements where it accelerates learning. The goal is to shrink the distance between an idea and validated business value. 
  • Systems thinker. Sees every feature as a node in a larger system rather than a standalone deliverable — thinking end-to-end from upstream inputs to downstream impact. Asks "how should the system behave to achieve the outcome?" rather than "what feature should we build?" Uses AI to model systems, expose hidden dependencies, generate edge cases, and evaluate downstream impacts before implementation begins.
  • Intelligent orchestrator. Treat AI as a reasoning partner that challenges assumptions, proposes alternatives, and automates routine coordination — synthesizing requirements, summarizing decisions, and surfacing risks — so your time is reinvested in ambiguous problems and strategic calls. 
  • Decision architect. Shifts from "is the requirement complete?" to "do we have evidence the solution will achieve the outcome?" Defines evals up front and lets data — not opinion — drive the call, generating evidence through business-rule simulation, scenario modeling, edge-case generation, and prototype validation. Correctness before code.

Increase Productivity with AI 

  • Apply AI to the product loop. Use AI to accelerate research, PRD generation, competitive analysis, user-feedback synthesis, and reporting — raising both the throughput and the quality of the product org. 
  • Build reusable leverage. Establish patterns, templates, and internal tools that make PMs and engineers across the team measurably more productive. 

Lead Across Teams
